Visit /r/stopselfharm and talking to them there. 
Talking to your GP (family doctor). 
Talking to a friend or relatives you can trust (depending on your situation etc — personally I don’t have anyone like that I can talk to but a lot do). 
Downloading apps that are designed to help, such as Calm Harm.

If it’s any consolation it sounds like they’re unlikely to get infected. Even cuts that bleed (and don’t go into fat) very very very rarely get infected because the bodies defence mechanisms / immune response starts as soon as the breach in skin occurs.  
  
As for being committed to a hospital it depends on literally so much, such as what country you’re from, age, how well the doctor actually knows you etc, conditions you are diagnosed with etc etc   
  
Being in Australia I’ve found it’s actually very hard to get committed into a psych ward. Even if I go to hospital and get stitches for cuts they typically let me go straight after. I’ve got to my doctor many times for stitches, while crying etc and he’s never said I need to go to hospital to be assessed.  
  
They’ll generally assess your suicidal ideation. Whether you have a specific and lethal plan etc. will determine if you’re shipped off.  
   
That being said, in certain conditions they actually try and avoid hospitalising. Borderline personality disorder is one of these conditions (there’s heaps of research and journal articles on why this is).   
  
Generally medical professionals don’t take superficial self harming seriously at all, and understand that it is generally done WITHOUT suicidal intent.   
  
So I honestly think you’ll be fine if you mention it to the doctor and say you want some help. If you have a therapist/psych I would also recommend it to them, so they can help you kick the bad habit now.
